title: MutableDataFrame.length needs a setter for cloneDeep-safety
answers: TypeError: Cannot set property length of #<d> which has only a getter
cloneDeep crashes on a DataFrame in Explore with Rspack/ESM build
Why does lodash cloneDeep throw on MutableDataFrame but not in Jest?
Plugin crashes calling cloneDeep(props.data) on a DataFrame
body:
Symptom: cloneDeep(mutableDataFrame) throws 'Cannot set property length ... which has only a getter' — only in strict-mode ESM bundles (e.g. Rspack), not in Jest (which transpiles lodash to CommonJS, non-strict).
Root cause: packages/grafana-data/src/dataframe/MutableDataFrame.ts MutableDataFrame.length was getter-only (derived from this.first.length); generic deep-clone utilities read a property then write it back onto the clone, which throws in strict mode when there's no setter.
Fix pattern: add a no-op setter alongside a derived/computed getter so generic object copiers (lodash cloneDeep, structuredClone-like utilities) can write back the value they read without throwing.
Constraints: apply this to any class with a getter-only property that may be visited by a generic deep-clone/copy routine; write a test that assigns the property directly (clone.length = 3) rather than via Jest's cloneDeep, since Jest's CommonJS lodash won't reproduce strict-mode failures.
applies: Any getter-only/derived property on classes (especially DataFrame implementations in grafana-data) that may be passed through generic object-copying utilities like lodash cloneDeep.

search: MutableDataFrame.length property requires both a getter and setter to prevent cloneDeep failures in strict-mode ESM bundles like Rspack. The property was getter-only (derived from this.first.length) in packages/grafana-data/src/dataframe/MutableDataFrame.ts, causing generic deep-clone utilities to throw 'Cannot set property length ... which has only a getter' when they read and write back the value. Add a no-op setter alongside the computed getter so lodash cloneDeep and similar utilities can write without throwing; Jest's CommonJS transpilation hides this, so test by assigning directly (clone.length = 3) rather than relying on Jest's cloneDeep. Applies to any getter-only derived property on classes (especially DataFrame implementations in grafana-data) that may pass through generic object-copying routines.
